name: BusUndervoltage Fault (Blown fuse)

name: MotorOvertemp Fault (Motor Overtemp)
also: Shown as E04 on the seven-segment display
meaning: The motor's thermal switch opened because the motor got too hot.
symptoms: Fault after running a while, or at once if the thermal circuit is open.
causes: Motor overloaded or ambient too hot; wiring fault in the thermal switch circuit; wrong motor selected in the drive; failed thermal switch.
checks: Feel whether the motor is hot; check the thermal switch wiring in the feedback cable.
repairable: Yes: motor thermal and winding repairs are routine.

name: DriveOvercurrent Fault (Power Fault)
also: Shown as E05 on the seven-segment display
meaning: The drive's Intelligent Power Module (IPM) shut down to protect itself from a major power fault.
symptoms: Fault at enable or during motion; often returns immediately after reset.
causes: Shorted motor cable or motor winding; failed power stage in the drive; drive overheating; running above the drive's continuous rating.
checks: With power off, megger the motor and cable to ground; check the drive's cooling.
repairable: Yes: power stage repair is a common Kinetix repair.
service: Servo drive repair; servo motor repair

name: HardOvertravel Fault (+/- Hard Overtravel)
also: Shown as E06 on the seven-segment display

name: MotFeedbackFault (Motor Feedback Loss)
also: Shown as E07 on the seven-segment display
meaning: The drive lost the motor feedback signal (open, shorted or missing wiring).
symptoms: Fault at power-up or when the cable flexes.
causes: Damaged feedback cable or connector; failed motor encoder; faulty feedback input on the drive.
checks: Inspect and reseat the feedback connector; check the cable for damage; try a known-good cable.
repairable: Yes: encoder and drive feedback repairs are standard.
service: Encoder repair; servo motor repair; servo drive repair

name: BusUndervoltage Fault (Bus Undervoltage)
also: Shown as E09 on the seven-segment display
meaning: The DC bus voltage fell below the minimum while three-phase power was present.
symptoms: Fault under load, on supply dips, or when an axis is enabled on a follower rail.
causes: Low or missing supply phase; supply dips; converter or bus capacitor problems in the IAM.
checks: Measure all three supply phases under load; check fuses and the main contactor.
repairable: Yes, when the IAM converter section is the cause.

name: DriveOvervoltage Fault (Bus Overvoltage)
also: Shown as E10 on the seven-segment display
meaning: The DC bus voltage rose above the limit, usually from too much regenerated energy.
symptoms: Fault during deceleration or when the load drives the motor.
causes: Deceleration too fast; shunt resistor or shunt module missing or failed; high supply voltage.
checks: Check the shunt module and resistor; note whether the fault happens during braking.
repairable: Often a setting or shunt issue; repairable when the drive's bus sensing is faulty.

name: GroundShortFault (Ground Fault)
also: Shown as E34 on the seven-segment display
meaning: The converter detected excessive current to ground.
symptoms: Fault at enable or as soon as main power is applied.
causes: Motor cable or winding ground fault; wiring error; internal drive fault.
checks: Disconnect the motor and megger the motor and cable to ground.
repairable: Yes: motor insulation repair or drive repair.
service: Servo motor repair; servo drive repair

name: DriveUndervoltage Fault (Precharge Fault)
also: Shown as E35 on the seven-segment display
meaning: The converter precharge cycle failed, so the DC bus did not charge correctly.
symptoms: The drive will not become ready after main power is applied.
causes: Low AC input voltage; failed precharge circuit inside the IAM.
checks: Measure the AC input voltage on all three phases.

name: DriveOvertemp Fault (Drive Overtemp)
also: Shown as E72 on the seven-segment display
meaning: The inverter's thermal switch tripped because the drive got too hot.
symptoms: Fault after running a while or in a hot cabinet.
causes: Failed IAM or AM fan; cabinet too hot; blocked airflow; duty cycle above the drive's continuous rating.
checks: Check the module fans; clean airflow paths; measure the cabinet temperature.
repairable: Yes: fan replacement and thermal repairs are routine.
service: Servo drive repair; cooling fan replacement
